references.text: Prohibition against profaning God's name by offering children to Molech, the same theme of not profaning God's holy name.
Prohibition against swearing falsely by God's name and thereby profaning it, the same concept of not profaning God's name.
Offering children to Molech profaned God's holy name, the same theme of the profanation of God's name.
The priests are to be holy and not profane their God's name, parallel to the prohibition against profaning God's name.
The Lord is the one who sanctifies Israel, the same statement that God is the one who sanctifies His people.
Israel profaned God's holy name among the nations, and God will sanctify His great name, the same theme of God's name and holiness.
God will show Himself holy in the eyes of the nations, the same theme that God is sanctified among the people.
The Lord of hosts is to be held holy, a parallel theme concerning sanctifying the Lord's name.
The children of Jacob are to keep Jacob's Holy One holy and fear the God of Israel, a theme about sanctifying God.
Jesus teaches His disciples to pray 'Let your name be kept holy', which echoes the command to sanctify God's name.
In the Lord's Prayer, one asks that God's name be kept holy, parallel to the sanctification of God's name.
Christians are urged to keep Christ holy as Lord in their hearts, a theme about sanctifying God.
